summary: The 2026-07-28 core protocol is composed of exactly three message patterns, all carried unchanged by every transport: (1) Request/Response: client sends a request, server answers with one result or error, optionally preceded by request-scoped notifications (notifications/progress, notifications/message). (2) Multi Round-Trip Requests: server answers with an InputRequiredResult and the client re-issues the request (new id) with inputResponses. (3) Subscribe-and-Notify: client sends subscriptions/listen; reply is a long-lived stream, first message per subscription is notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, all stream messages carry _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId"] = listen request id; stream state is request-scoped and re-issued after channel loss. Only the client initiates: servers MUST NOT send JSON-RPC requests; clients never send responses. Cancellation is transport-dependent: on Streamable HTTP closing the per-request SSE stream IS the cancellation (server MUST treat disconnect as cancel, no notifications/cancelled expected); on stdio the client MUST send notifications/cancelled {requestId, reason?}. Servers MUST send notifications/cancelled only to tear down a subscriptions/listen stream (stdio) and MUST NOT use it otherwise. Cancellation is best-effort: receivers SHOULD stop work, free resources and not respond; MAY ignore unknown/completed/uncancellable requests; both sides MUST handle races; clients SHOULD ignore late responses; invalid notifications SHOULD be ignored. Timeouts SHOULD exist per request, be configurable, MAY reset on progress but SHOULD have a hard maximum. Progress: client opts in via params._meta.progressToken (string|number, unique across active requests); server MAY emit notifications/progress {progressToken, progress (monotonically increasing, may be float), total?, message?}; only for active tokens; MUST stop after completion; both sides SHOULD track tokens and rate-limit. Progress notifications travel only on the originating request's response stream (HTTP) and never carry subscriptionId.

methods.name: notifications/cancelled
methods.direction: notification c->s (primary); notification s->c ONLY on stdio to terminate a subscriptions/listen stream
methods.params: params: CancelledNotificationParams { requestId: RequestId (string|number) — REQUIRED (non-optional in 2026-07-28 schema.ts L626; 'MUST correspond to the ID of a request the client previously issued'); reason?: string — optional, 'MAY be logged or presented to the user'; _meta?: NotificationMetaObject (inherited from NotificationParams; no reserved key is defined for this notification) }
methods.result: none (notification). No response is sent for the cancelled request itself (server SHOULD not respond; client SHOULD ignore any late response).
methods.capability_gate: None. Not gated by any capability; part of the core protocol. Schema unions: ClientNotification = CancelledNotification (the ONLY client notification in 2026-07-28, schema.ts L3166); ServerNotification includes CancelledNotification (L3175).
methods.notes: Transport rule (cancellation.md 'Transport-Specific Cancellation'; stdio.md 'Cancellation'; streamable-http.md 'Cancellation' + Note L92-102): on stdio the client MUST send this notification to cancel; on Streamable HTTP it is NOT required or expected — closing the SSE response stream is the cancellation signal, and the HTTP page states the core protocol defines no client-to-server notifications over Streamable HTTP (header requirements for notification POSTs are undefined). Server-sent usage (cancellation.md L13-16, Behavior Requirements #2; schema.ts L637): requestId MUST be the id of a subscriptions/listen request; used solely to tear down that subscription stream; MUST NOT be used for any other purpose. Race semantics: may arrive after completion; both sides MUST handle gracefully. The 2025-xx text 'A client MUST NOT attempt to cancel its initialize request' is absent in 2026-07-28 (there is no initialize request in this revision).

methods.name: notifications/progress
methods.params: params: ProgressNotificationParams { progressToken: ProgressToken (string|number) — REQUIRED, must equal the token supplied in the originating request's params._meta.progressToken; progress: number — REQUIRED, MUST increase with each notification even if total unknown, MAY be floating point; total?: number — optional, MAY be floating point, omitted if unknown; message?: string — optional, SHOULD be relevant human-readable progress info; _meta?: NotificationMetaObject — 'io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId' is ABSENT on progress notifications (schema.ts L126-128) }
methods.capability_gate: None. Opt-in is per request via params._meta.progressToken (RequestMetaObject.progressToken?: ProgressToken, schema.ts L67; basic__index.md _meta table L354). 'The receiver is not obligated to provide these notifications.' Only in ServerNotification union (schema.ts L3176); NOT in ClientNotification in 2026-07-28.
methods.notes: Delivery scoping: on Streamable HTTP, delivered only on the SSE response stream of the originating request, never on a subscriptions/listen stream (streamable-http.md L109-113, L129-131); on stdio, written to stdout as an in-flight-request notification (stdio.md L49-50). Timeout interaction: receivers MAY reset a request timeout on progress but SHOULD keep a maximum timeout (cancellation.md 'Timeouts').

methods.name: subscriptions/listen (as referenced by the patterns index and cancellation page; full definition on the subscriptions page)
methods.params: params: SubscriptionsListenRequestParams { _meta: RequestMetaObject (required, incl. io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities); notifications: SubscriptionFilter (required; server MUST NOT send notification types not explicitly requested) }
methods.result: SubscriptionsListenResult { resultType: 'complete'; _meta: SubscriptionsListenResultMetaObject { 'io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId': RequestId (required; equals the response id) } } — sent ONLY when the server tears the subscription down gracefully; otherwise the stream stays open and no response is sent. Stream messages: first message per subscription id MUST be notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged { notifications: SubscriptionFilter }, then the opted-in notifications/* each carrying _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId'].
methods.capability_gate: None stated on the patterns pages; not a declared capability.
methods.notes: Included here because cancellation semantics reference it: client ends it by closing the SSE stream (HTTP) or notifications/cancelled referencing the listen request id (stdio); server ends it by SHOULD sending the success response then closing (HTTP) or, on stdio, MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the listen request id (cancellation.md L13-16; schema.ts L637). Stream state is scoped to the request; on channel loss the client re-issues subscriptions/listen (patterns index L67-69; subscriptions.md L162-164).

requirements.text: Servers MUST NOT initiate JSON-RPC requests; clients do not send JSON-RPC responses. Every interaction begins with the client.
While a request is in flight the server MAY send notifications scoped to it (notifications/progress, notifications/message) before the response.

For Subscribe-and-Notify, stream state is scoped to the subscriptions/listen request; if the underlying channel is lost the client re-issues the request (on stdio reconnection the client MUST re-send subscriptions/listen; server holds no subscription state).
requirements.cite: patterns/index.md 'Subscribe and Notify' L62-69; subscriptions.md 'Graceful Closure' L162-164

requirements.text: A client SHOULD send a cancellation notification to indicate that a request it previously issued should be terminated (when it wants it terminated; transport rules below govern the concrete signal).
A server MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing a subscriptions/listen request ID when it tears down that subscription stream (stdio).
requirements.cite: cancellation.md L13-15; Behavior Requirements #2 L73-74; schema.ts L637

requirements.text: Servers MUST NOT send notifications/cancelled for any other purpose than terminating a subscriptions/listen stream.
requirements.cite: cancellation.md L15-16; schema.ts L637 'Servers MUST NOT use this notification to cancel any other request.'

requirements.text: Streamable HTTP: the server MUST treat a client disconnect (closing the SSE response stream) as cancellation of that request; no notifications/cancelled is required or expected.
After a request is cancelled (HTTP stream closed or stdio notifications/cancelled), the server MUST NOT send any further messages for it, and SHOULD stop work as soon as practical.
stdio: to cancel an in-flight request the client MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the request ID (there is no per-request stream to close).

Cancellation notifications MUST only reference requests that were previously issued by the client and are believed to still be in-progress (params.requestId MUST correspond to a request the client previously issued).
requirements.cite: cancellation.md Behavior Requirements #1 L70-72; schema.ts L622-626

requirements.text: Servers receiving cancellation notifications SHOULD stop processing the cancelled request, free associated resources, and not send a response for the cancelled request.
requirements.cite: cancellation.md Behavior Requirements #3 L75-78; schema.ts L641

requirements.text: Servers MAY ignore cancellation notifications if the referenced request is unknown, processing has already completed, or the request cannot be cancelled.
The client SHOULD ignore any response to the cancelled request that arrives afterward.
Both parties MUST handle cancellation race conditions gracefully (notification may arrive after processing completed and after a response was already sent).
Invalid cancellation notifications SHOULD be ignored: unknown request IDs, already completed requests, malformed notifications (fire-and-forget; no error response).
Both parties SHOULD log cancellation reasons for debugging; application UIs SHOULD indicate when cancellation is requested.

Implementations SHOULD establish timeouts for all sent requests; when no success/error response arrives within the timeout the sender SHOULD cancel the request (HTTP: close the response stream; stdio: send notifications/cancelled) and stop waiting.
SDKs and other middleware SHOULD allow request timeouts to be configured on a per-request basis.
Implementations MAY reset the timeout clock when receiving a progress notification for the request.
Implementations SHOULD always enforce a maximum timeout regardless of progress notifications.
The server MAY send progress notifications to report status of requests the client issued; it is not obligated to (may send none, at any frequency, may omit total).
requirements.cite: progress.md L10-11, L35, Behavior Requirements #2 L66-69; schema.ts L65

requirements.text: Progress tokens MUST be a string or integer value (ProgressToken = string | number) and MUST be unique across all active requests.
The progress value MUST increase with each notification, even if the total is unknown; progress and total MAY be floating point.
The message field SHOULD provide relevant human-readable progress information.
Progress notifications MUST only reference tokens that were provided in an active request and are associated with an in-progress operation.
Progress notifications MUST stop after completion of the request.
Clients and servers SHOULD track active progress tokens.
Both parties SHOULD implement rate limiting of progress notifications to prevent flooding.

Streamable HTTP: notifications sent on a request's SSE response stream MUST relate to the originating client request; request-scoped notifications (progress, message) are NOT delivered on the subscriptions/listen stream.

The server MUST include _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId'] on every notification delivered via a subscriptions/listen stream; the key is absent on progress notifications for in-flight requests.
requirements.cite: schema.ts NotificationMetaObject L120-134; stdio.md L51-55; basic/index.md L415

requirements.text: stdio: clients MUST correlate subscription-stream notifications using _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId'].

notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged MUST be the first message the server sends carrying a given subscriptionId; the server MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before acknowledging it (ordering is per subscription id, not per channel, on stdio).

When the server ends a subscription on its own initiative it SHOULD respond to the original subscriptions/listen request with a success result (resultType 'complete', _meta subscriptionId) before closing the stream (HTTP); on stdio the MUST for notifications/cancelled applies.
requirements.cite: subscriptions.md 'Cancellation'/'Graceful Closure' L124-126, L132-138; cancellation.md L13-15

wire_details: CancelledNotificationParams: requestId: RequestId (string | number, REQUIRED); reason?: string. Example: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/cancelled","params":{"requestId":"123","reason":"User requested cancellation"}} (cancellation.md L26-35).

ProgressNotificationParams: progressToken: string|number (REQUIRED); progress: number (REQUIRED, JSON number, may be float); total?: number; message?: string. Example: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/progress","params":{"progressToken":"abc123","progress":50,"total":100,"message":"Reticulating splines..."}} (progress.md L42-53).

Request opt-in key: params._meta.progressToken (string | number) — a plain (non-prefixed) reserved _meta key listed in the basic/index.md reserved-keys table L354 alongside io.modelcontextprotocol/* keys. Example: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"some_method","params":{"_meta":{"progressToken":"abc123"}}} (progress.md L22-33).

_meta key: "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId" (value: RequestId = JSON-RPC id of the subscriptions/listen request) — present on every subscription-stream notification and on the SubscriptionsListenResult; absent on progress notifications (schema.ts L133, L1334).
JSON-RPC: jsonrpc = "2.0"; RequestId = string | number; notifications have no id; JSONRPCErrorResponse.id is optional (schema.ts L261-302).
No error codes are defined by the cancellation or progress pages: invalid/late cancellation notifications are silently ignored, never answered with a JSON-RPC error (cancellation.md L115-122).

No HTTP headers are defined for cancellation or progress. Streamable HTTP cancellation = client closes the SSE response stream (Content-Type: text/event-stream) of that request; the spec states header requirements for notification POSTs are not defined by this revision and notifications/cancelled is not expected over HTTP (streamable-http.md L92-102).

Streamable HTTP servers SHOULD send X-Accel-Buffering: no on SSE streams so progress notifications are not buffered by proxies (streamable-http.md L133-139). Last-Event-ID / resumable SSE is NOT supported (L152).
stdio framing: one JSON message per line on stdout/stdin, single shared channel, no per-request streams; server MUST NOT write JSON-RPC requests to stdout (stdio.md L43-57).

Schema unions (2026-07-28): ClientNotification = CancelledNotification only; ServerNotification = CancelledNotification | ProgressNotification | ... | SubscriptionsAcknowledgedNotification (schema.ts L3166-3182).
sdk_implications: Client core: per-request timeout (configurable per call, with a global default and a hard maximum ceiling), optional reset-on-progress; on timeout perform transport-appropriate cancellation and reject the pending promise/task locally.

Client core: expose Cancel(requestId, reason?) / CancellationToken integration. Transport abstraction must expose a 'cancel signal' primitive: stdio transport sends notifications/cancelled {requestId, reason}; Streamable HTTP transport aborts the in-flight HTTP request/SSE stream and sends no notification. The SDK must never emit notifications/cancelled over Streamable HTTP.

Client core: keep a pending-request table keyed by RequestId; after local cancellation mark the entry so late responses/errors and further notifications for that id are discarded (no exception, log at debug).

Client core: progress opt-in API per request (e.g. -ProgressAction/callback); SDK generates progressToken values (string or integer) guaranteed unique across active requests (e.g. monotonically increasing counter or GUID); inject into params._meta.progressToken; dispatch incoming notifications/progress by progressToken to the callback; drop notifications for unknown/completed tokens; remove token when response arrives; optional rate-limit/coalescing.

Client core: validate incoming notifications/progress (progressToken required, progress required numeric, total/message optional) and notifications/cancelled from server; server-sent notifications/cancelled is only valid when requestId matches an active subscriptions/listen request — then end that subscription locally (and optionally auto-resubscribe); ignore otherwise.
Client core: never send a JSON-RPC response; never accept JSON-RPC requests from the server (server->client interactions come only via InputRequiredResult per MRTR).

Server core: maintain a table of in-flight requests keyed by RequestId with a per-request cancellation token; stdio transport: on notifications/cancelled look up requestId, trigger the token, suppress the eventual response (do not write a result/error for a cancelled request), free resources; ignore unknown/completed/malformed silently (log reason). Streamable HTTP transport: wire the HTTP connection-aborted/SSE-closed event to the same cancellation token; after cancellation suppress all further messages for that request.

Server core: expose a per-request context object to handlers carrying CancellationToken, the progressToken (if any), and a ReportProgress(progress, total?, message?) method that (a) is a no-op when no token was supplied, (b) enforces monotonic increase (reject or clamp non-increasing values), (c) stops emitting once the handler completes/cancels, (d) optionally rate-limits, (e) routes the notification to the originating request's response stream (HTTP) or stdout (stdio) and never onto a subscription stream, and never adds io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId.

Server core: notifications/cancelled emission API restricted to subscription teardown on stdio (referencing the listen request id); on HTTP send the SubscriptionsListenResult (resultType 'complete', _meta subscriptionId) then close the stream. Refuse/assert against any other server-side use.

Both: implement the three patterns generically in the protocol layer (request/response with request-scoped notifications; MRTR retry with inputResponses; long-lived listen streams with per-subscription ordering) so transports need only framing/delivery, per patterns/index.md 'Adding Patterns'.
Both: message validation must reject notifications/cancelled lacking requestId (required in 2026-07-28) unless operating in a legacy (2025-11-25) mode where it was optional for task cancellation.
Logging: log cancellation reasons and cancelled request ids on both sides; surface 'cancellation requested' state to host UIs (Write-Progress in PowerShell maps naturally to progress notifications).

Conformance: the tools-call-with-progress scenario exists in the conformance suite (conformance_README.md L198, SDK_INTEGRATION.md L76); the server SDK must correctly emit progress for tools/call when a progressToken is supplied.
legacy_delta: Direction: 2025-06-18/2025-11-25 allowed notifications/cancelled to be sent by EITHER side for any previously-issued request in the same direction (servers could cancel their own sampling/elicitation/roots requests). 2026-07-28: clients cancel their requests; servers send it ONLY to tear down a subscriptions/listen stream on stdio and MUST NOT use it for anything else (there are no server-initiated requests any more).

requestId optionality: 2025-11-25 CancelledNotificationParams.requestId was optional (omitted when cancelling tasks via tasks/cancel; 'MUST NOT be used for cancelling tasks'). 2026-07-28: requestId is required; tasks and tasks/cancel do not exist in the 2026-07-28 schema.

initialize rule: 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 stated 'A client MUST NOT attempt to cancel its initialize request'. 2026-07-28 has no initialize request/lifecycle; the rule is gone. A dual-era SDK must keep the guard only in legacy mode.

Transport semantics: earlier revisions had no transport-specific cancellation rule; notifications/cancelled was the universal mechanism over both stdio and HTTP. 2026-07-28: over Streamable HTTP closing the per-request SSE stream IS the cancellation and notifications/cancelled is not expected (core protocol defines no client->server notifications over HTTP); notifications/cancelled is stdio-only.

Schema unions: 2025-xx ClientNotification also included InitializedNotification, ProgressNotification, RootsListChangedNotification; ServerNotification included CancelledNotification/ProgressNotification for server-initiated requests. 2026-07-28: ClientNotification = CancelledNotification only; ProgressNotification is server->client only (clients no longer receive requests, so they never report progress).

Progress: ProgressToken type (string|number), progressToken location (params._meta.progressToken) and ProgressNotificationParams fields (progressToken, progress, total?, message?) are unchanged across 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. New in 2026-07-28: _meta is a typed RequestMetaObject where io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities are REQUIRED on every request alongside the optional progressToken; NotificationMetaObject gained io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId (absent on progress notifications).

Timeout text (SHOULD establish timeouts, per-request configurability, MAY reset on progress, SHOULD enforce maximum) is carried over from 2025-xx; new is the explicit mapping of timeout-triggered cancellation to 'close the HTTP response stream' vs 'send notifications/cancelled on stdio'.
Progress race/behavior rules (tokens active only, MUST increase, MUST stop after completion, rate limiting, tracking) are unchanged from 2025-11-25.
open_questions: Streamable HTTP: the spec says notifications/cancelled is 'not expected' over HTTP but does not say a server MUST reject or MUST ignore one if a client POSTs it; header requirements for notification POSTs are explicitly undefined. Decide whether the PowerShell HTTP server silently accepts (202) and ignores it, or treats it as an ordinary notification POST.

Server-sent notifications/cancelled on Streamable HTTP: cancellation.md L13-15 phrases the MUST without a transport qualifier, while schema.ts L637 and subscriptions.md scope it to stdio (HTTP uses the SubscriptionsListenResult + stream close). Treat as stdio-only; confirm against TypeScript SDK v2 behavior.

Progress before acknowledgement/after cancellation: the spec says progress MUST stop 'after completion' but does not define behavior for progress emitted between a cancellation signal and handler exit; SDK should suppress (consistent with 'MUST NOT send any further messages').

Uniqueness of progressToken 'across all active requests' — scope is per client/session; unclear whether uniqueness must hold across multiple concurrent sessions of one server process (SDK should key tokens per session).
progress monotonicity enforcement: spec does not state receiver behavior for a non-increasing progress value (ignore? accept?). SDK receiver should accept and log; sender should enforce.
No guidance on what to do with a progressToken supplied on subscriptions/listen (long-lived request); presumably allowed but meaningless; SDK may ignore.
Rate limiting thresholds for progress are unspecified (SHOULD only) — choose a default (e.g. coalesce to at most N/s) and make it configurable.
